answers.text: Use of ultrasound in pregnancy before 20 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Act does not prohibit obstetric ultrasound — it permits it for legitimate medical indications. The prohibition is specifically on sex determination and selective sex-based abortion.

answers.text: Sex determination of a foetus and sex-selective abortion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act 1994 (amended 2002) prohibits communication of fetal sex and sex-selective termination, to combat female foeticide and the resulting skewed sex ratio.

answers.text: Performing ultrasound examinations without an AERB licence

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: AERB regulates ionising radiation; diagnostic ultrasound licensing under PC-PNDT is administered by the Appropriate Authority, not AERB.
While the Act regulates accreditation of pre-natal diagnostic facilities, its primary prohibition is specifically sex determination and sex-selective abortion.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. The PC-PNDT Act 1994 specifically prohibits prenatal sex determination and sex-selective abortion. Obstetric ultrasound for legitimate clinical indications is fully permitted.
Correct! PC-PNDT prohibits communicating fetal sex and sex-selective abortion — its aim is to stop female foeticide and correct the declining sex ratio.
